“Pupils receive a warm welcome every day…. and benefit from staff expertise and impressive leadership,” says Ofsted We are delighted to share Forest Academy’s latest Ofsted report with our community. The inspectors visited us on 14 and 15 July 2026 and have delivered a very positive report from their two day inspection.
Welcome to our School
Welcome to Forest Academy, a vibrant, inclusive primary school set within eight acres of green space in Shirley. We are proud to serve a diverse and dynamic community, offering a high-quality, values-led education where every child is known, supported and inspired to thrive.
At Forest, our core values — kindness, respect, resilience, responsibility, collaboration and curiosity —are woven into daily life. We nurture confident, compassionate learners who think critically, act with integrity and see themselves as leaders of the future.
We are proud to be recognised as a Nurturing Schools Award holder and a Healthy Relationships Champion School. As an IQM Flagship School for Inclusion and a DfE Attendance & Behaviour Hub, we place wellbeing, equity and opportunity at the heart of everything we do.
Our rich global curriculum, inclusive culture and strong community partnerships ensure every pupil can flourish academically, socially and emotionally. As part of the Inspire Partnership, we collaborate widely to offer the very best to every child and family.
We hope this website gives you a glimpse of what makes Forest Academy special. If you’d like to visit or find out more, please don’t hesitate to get in touch — we’d love to welcome you.

“Pupils receive a warm welcome every day…. and benefit from staff expertise and impressive leadership,” says Ofsted
We are delighted to share Forest Academy’s latest Ofsted report with our community.
The inspectors visited us on 14 and 15 July 2026 and have delivered a very positive report from their two day inspection.
We received the rating Strong Standard for pupil achievement, attendance and behaviour, curriculum and teaching, early years provision, our work to ensure all pupils are included regardless of any barriers they face, and personal development and wellbeing.
Our Academy’s leadership and its governance was particularly praised and given an Exceptional rating. This is a rating given to very few schools across the country, intended to reward schools and trusts that are performing at the very highest level nationally.
The report says, “The impact of leaders' rigorous tracking of pupils' vulnerabilities is tangible. This means that leaders make decisions with pupils' needs at the heart of everything. Pupils, including the most vulnerable, have access to an excellent education.”
Rupinder Bansil, Headteacher at Forest Academy, said, “We are delighted to have received such a glowing report. Staff, pupils and parents should be incredibly proud of what this report shows we achieve together every school day.”
Other highlights from the report include recognition of the school’s unwavering commitment to inclusion and community engagement, its culture of excellent behaviour and its high aspirations for all pupils.
The report describes early years as being “full of the purposeful buzz of learning” and recognises the extensive opportunities offered through Forest’s global curriculum and personal development provision.

Inspire Partnership
Forest Academy is part of Inspire Partnership, a small multi-academy trust working in Croydon, Greenwich, and Medway to transform students’ lives.
As a partnership of schools, we are better able to support our students. We strongly believe in the power of collaboration and continually work together to find innovative ways of working.
The Partnership
Our partnership of schools are Forest Academy, West Thornton, Woodside, Foxfield, Rockliffe Manor, Woodhill, Delce, Chattenden, Elaine and Maundene. Our schools all have their own identity and are separate schools. However, we work together to have similar visions and values and continually collaborate behind the scenes to help us benchmark our standards and work together to improve the teaching and learning for all our children. Our partnership is led by CEO Rob Carpenter who works across all our schools supporting our school-based headteachers and a central team of executive leaders and central office staff who are deployed to work across all schools within our MAT.
Working in partnership, sharing practice and showcasing outstanding teaching and learning helps us raise our expectations and continually look for ways we can improve. We know we are stronger together and it enables us to offer the very best to the students and staff of our schools. To better understand our partnership of schools and how we work together, look to the Inspire Partnership website.
A key area of focus across our partnership of schools is to ensure consistent and quality teaching and learning. We are dedicated to supporting and developing our staff across our schools to ensure the best for our students. Some ways in which our schools work together are:
Inspire Partnership is a national leader of school improvement support, we work both within our wider communities in Croydon, Greenwich and Medway but also nationally to deliver training, host school visits and provide school improvement support. Our programmes for school improvement enable us to make wider impact and work in genuine collaboration. Through this we aim to:
We are always seeking out more opportunities to work with more schools and provide new and exciting opportunities for teachers and leaders to learn from each other. Do get in touch if you are interested in finding out more.

PE & Sports Premium
At Forest Academy, we are committed to helping every child lead a healthy, active lifestyle. Our PE and Sports Premium funding is used to develop high-quality PE, expand access to diverse sporting activities, and promote wellbeing, teamwork, and personal growth through physical education.
We ensure that every pupil, regardless of ability, has the opportunity to participate, progress, and succeed in sport and physical activity.
Nature of Provision
Our Sports Premium supports a wide range of initiatives, including:
Weekly PE lessons led by a specialist sports coach for all pupils
Regular CPD for teaching staff, improving planning, delivery, and confidence in PE
A strong partnership with the Palace for Life Foundation (Crystal Palace FC) delivering sessions that promote fitness, teamwork, resilience and leadership
Membership in the Croydon Schools Sports Partnership (CSSP), providing access to competitions, staff training, and inter-school collaboration
Expansion of our after-school sports clubs, based on pupil interest (e.g. girls’ football, basketball)
Development of Play Leaders, who support lunchtime activities and lead games for younger children
Celebratory events such as Sports Day and Health Awareness Week, engaging families and local clubs in promoting healthy lifestyles
Curriculum & Staff Development
Our curriculum is designed to:
Offer a broad range of physical activities: gymnastics, dance, athletics, team sports, swimming, and more
Build progression in skills, confidence, and sporting knowledge
Promote cross-curricular learning and whole-child development
Encourage all staff to grow in confidence and capability through coaching and CPD opportunities
Use PE as a platform to teach character traits like fairness, resilience, and leadership
Impact of Sports Premium Funding (2024–25)
Increased pupil engagement in physical activity during lessons, lunch, and after school
Strong uptake in sports clubs and improved access to competitive opportunities
Enhanced pupil confidence and skill development across a range of sports
Increased staff confidence and quality of PE teaching through specialist input
Positive feedback and pupil outcomes from Palace for Life sessions
Greater pupil leadership and responsibility through the Play Leaders programme
A highly successful Health Awareness Week, showcasing sport, wellbeing, and community partnerships
Priorities for 2025–26
For the upcoming year, we aim to:
Continue expanding our after-school and lunchtime physical activity offer
Deepen our collaboration with Palace for Life Foundation
Maximise our involvement in CSSP competitions and professional development
Increase visibility of sport and physical wellbeing across the curriculum and school community
Strengthen transitions into local clubs for children showing sporting potential

Vision and Ethos
Ethos
At Forest Academy, we are committed to ensuring that no child is left behind. We believe every child has the right to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally — whatever their background, needs or starting point. Our culture is one of high expectations, nurture, and equity, built on the firm belief that every child can succeed.
As part of the Inspire Partnership, we provide an inclusive, ambitious curriculum and a safe, nurturing environment where children gain essential knowledge, skills, and confidence. We empower pupils to find their voice, discover their passions, and contribute positively to their community and the wider world.
Core values
Our school values are embedded in every aspect of school life, from the way we learn and play, to how we lead and grow together. They guide our interactions, shape our learning behaviours, and reflect the kind of citizens we aspire to develop.
We believe that partnership with parents and carers is integral to our success. Families are not just welcomed, they are valued collaborators in our shared mission to provide the best possible education for every child.
At Forest, children thrive when they feel happy, safe and respected. Through our nurturing ethos, inclusive practices, and deep commitment to community, we foster a strong sense of belonging and purpose for all.
